chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from his father, from Abi Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

If a salat (prayer) has passed you by and you remember it at the time of another, then if you know that, were you to perform the one that has passed you by, you would still be within the time of the other, then begin with the one that has passed you by.
For Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “Establish the salat (prayer) for My remembrance.”
And if you know that, if you perform the one that has passed you by, the one after it would also pass you by, then begin with the one whose time you are in, and make up the other.

key_terms.فَاتَتْكَ: was missed by you or passed you by
key_terms.لِذِكْرِي: for My remembrance, cited from the Qur'an as proof
key_terms.وَقْتٍ: the legally designated time of a salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: If I remember a missed obligatory salat (prayer) during the time of another prayer, which one should I perform first?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who remembers a missed obligatory salat (prayer) during the time of another obligatory salat (prayer). If there is enough time to perform the missed salat (prayer) and still catch the current one within its time, the missed one is performed first; otherwise, the current salat (prayer) is performed first and the missed one is made up later.
